mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in WORKPLACES mobility reduces discretionary foot traffic around offices and nearby shops, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks as commuting-linked purchases fade.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below its current level for at least three of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and TRANSIT remains depressed, households substitute toward staying home and cut back on discretionary shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC falls within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains at least 15 points below t-3w while RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks despite TRANSIT staying deeply negative and RESIDENTIAL staying above 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in TRANSIT stations mobility acts as a proxy for tighter movement constraints; if transit use stays near current depressed levels, retail visits contract over the next four weeks because trip chaining becomes less feasible.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -45 and stays there for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -45 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM reflects weekend outing and errands intensity, which spills into retail and recreation spending and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days even though PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both rise from their current levels.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES remains weak but GROCERY_PHARM is relatively less negative, retail demand shifts toward necessity shopping rather than leisure shopping, keeping RETAIL_REC below the last four-week mean over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES stays below -25 while GROCERY_PHARM stays above -12
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite WORKPLACES remaining below -25 and GROCERY_PHARM remaining above -12.

mechanism_narrative: The steady rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates more time spent at home; if this intensifies further, discretionary shopping trips are displaced and RETAIL_REC falls over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL keeps increasing week over week.

mechanism_narrative: After a TRANSIT shock, retail weakens first and then recovers only if mobility normalizes; with TRANSIT still far below baseline, the next week's RETAIL_REC change should remain negative or flat.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases next week while TRANSIT remains below -40.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a recovery in PARKS combined with a smaller pullback in GROCERY_PHARM signals broader weekend activity that can spill into shopping districts and raise RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its last-four-week mean over the next 14 days even as PARKS improves and GROCERY_PHARM stops falling.
